column1: # The coverage authority for GPU serialization. One row per entry point that
# names a CUDA-opening command or a local wrapper of one -- llama-server,
# llama-bench, llama-cli, llama-mtmd-cli, llama-quantize, nsys, ncu, the pinned
# image runtime, and vulkan-graphics-service-probe -- so a new entry point that
# reaches the device is a missing row rather than an unserialized client. A
# regular expression over the tree grew a name at a time and answered nothing
# about which authority a script takes; this file answers that per entry point
# role states what the entry point is. `serving-session` and
# `measurement-campaign` are the two top-level orchestrators, and exactly one of
# them holds the owner lock at a time. `nested-orchestrator` launches a
# top-level owner and drives it without holding a claim, which is what an
# admission harness across the tmux boundary has to do. `active-workload`
# executes compute under an owner and takes the compute lease around it.
# `authorized-monitor` observes the device under an owner without running
# compute; the graphics-latency probe belongs here rather than in the desktop
# pattern, because its submissions are project-generated traffic even on the
# graphics queue. `non-gpu-helper` names a device binary and reaches none.
# top_level_owner    the entry point calls gpu_ownership_require as the owner.
#                    it verifies an inherited QWEN_GPU_OWNERSHIP_FD when one is
#                    present rather than opening a second claim.
#                    yes takes QWEN_GPU_COMPUTE_LEASE around its compute,
#                    exports names the file for the process that will take it.
#                    it may run beside other compute under one owner.
#                    its long-lived children are launched with `9>&-`. The rule
#                    is asymmetric by role: a campaign's server must close it or
#                    the claim outlives the campaign, and n-a marks an entry
#                    point that leaves no long-lived child behind.
# execution_policy   acquires, inherits, delegates, monitored, or none.
